A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3D-GSW by the same authors, with a shared watermarking framework despite substantial revisions. All pages, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. Both supplied PDFs end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark extraction, rendering-quality, image-attack, ablation, and optimization-time results on Blender and LLFF in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on Blender, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF 360, including image and model attacks, component ablations, pruning sensitivity, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: v1's FGD splits contributing Gaussians in high-frequency regions. v2 adds contribution-based pruning before splitting and revises the contribution calculation using an error-weighted auxiliary loss with zeroed color parameters (Sections 3.3–3.4). This changes the initialization procedure substantially. The exponential gradient mask and high-frequency wavelet loss already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 retains Blender and LLFF and adds Mip-NeRF 360, extending coverage to large, unbounded scenes. It also adds direct model-tampering scenarios through parameter noise and Gaussian removal. v1 evaluates rendered-image attacks; its standalone brightness attack is absent from v2.

E2.justification: In Tables 1–2, v2 removes CopyRNeRF, WateRF+NeRF, and WateRF+TensoRF, retains WateRF+3D-GS, and adds StegaNeRF+3D-GS. The without-FGD variant, already present in v1's ablations, also becomes a comparator in the main benchmark and attack tables.

E3.justification: Message lengths change from 16/32/48 to 32/48/64 bits; image-attack and component-ablation tables switch from 16 to 32 bits. Reported scaling changes from 25% to 75%, JPEG quality from 10% to 50%, and loss weights are revised. New protocols include 20% random Gaussian removal and parameter noise with sigma 0.1. v2 inconsistently specifies noise versus blur in its combined attack.

E4.justification: v2 adds model-attack robustness tests, an exponential-versus-nonexponential gradient-mask case study (Figure 7), and pruning-threshold sensitivity (Figure 8). Component and wavelet-subband ablations remain under revised settings. v1's zero/nonzero-contribution rendering demonstration and optimization-convergence plot are not retained as equivalent analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five different seeds and report dataset-averaged point estimates. Neither supplies confidence intervals, variability estimates, significance tests, or uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: The main result tables are replaced under revised coverage and settings. For example, the 32-bit 3D-GSW entry changes from 96.70% bit accuracy and 34.89 PSNR to 97.37% and 35.08; these are not comparable-setting gains. v2 adds 64-bit results, model-attack accuracies of 89.11% under noise and 96.87% after 20% Gaussian removal, and FPS/storage results. The 16-bit results disappear.

T1.justification: Mathematical revisions concentrate on contribution scoring: v1 Equation 8 uses an unweighted image-sum auxiliary loss, whereas v2 Equations 3–4 introduce error weighting, spatial normalization, a zeroed-color construction, and a revised gradient expression. The exponential-mask formula remains algebraically equivalent; expanded DFT and loss formulas mostly explain existing operations. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes being the first 3D-GS watermarking method and increasing capacity through densification. v2 drops the first-attempt assertion and makes pruning-enabled rendering speed and robustness to model distortion central contributions. Invisible watermarking and state-of-the-art performance claims remain, but FGD's claimed role is substantially redefined.

C2.justification: v2 explains robustness through concentrating watermark embedding in influential Gaussians and reframes the mask around limiting parameter changes and avoiding division by zero. It adds over-pruning discussion, although the prose says LPIPS decreases while Figure 8 shows an increase. v1's Gaussian-count memory limitation is removed; the decoder-pretraining limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies LL2 decoding, mask application to color/opacity/rotation/scale, the 1e-8 pruning threshold, and a 1e-4 parameter workaround for StegaNeRF. These disclosures do not establish that previously unspecified choices changed. Hardware changes from an RTX 3090 to an A100, loss coefficients are updated, and v1's explicit PyTorch/CUDA implementation statement is omitted.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the research positioning, adding a dedicated frequency-transform discussion and distinguishing robust watermarking from steganography, including GS-hider. Much of v1's mesh and generative-model watermarking discussion, including Deep 3D-to-2D and Stable Signature, disappears. This accompanies removal of the first-3D-GS-watermarking claim, beyond ordinary bibliography updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Method exposition expands from three subsections to six, moving rendering preliminaries out of related work and separating contribution measurement and losses. Limitations move into the conclusion, and the title changes to emphasize robust watermarking.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially redraws the visual presentation. The two original method diagrams are consolidated into Figure 2, while a new ownership/attack schematic becomes Figure 1. Qualitative comparison panels are redesigned, several difference maps change from 10× to 2×, and new model-attack and efficiency tables accompany replacement analysis plots.

improvement.justification: v1 claims protection of the model but tests watermark robustness only through rendered-image attacks. v2 directly tests model tampering (Table 3), while pruning sensitivity and FPS/storage measurements (Figure 8 and Table 6) substantiate the efficiency mechanism on larger scenes. These additions substantially strengthen evidence for central practical claims. Narrower baseline coverage and localized reporting errors, including the combined-attack mismatch and reversed LPIPS description, temper but do not outweigh these gains.
